# Poisson Regression

## Problem 1(20 points)

### Predicting football games using Poisson regression.

1. Make predictions for the same game from the same league assigned to you in homework 1, but now use the poisson regression model instead of distributions.**(8 points)**


```{r,echo=F}
england_home_2022 <- f_data_sm %>%
  filter(SEASON == "2022", COUNTRY == "England") %>%
  group_by(HOMETEAM) %>%
  summarise(MEAN_FTHG = mean(FTHG))

england_away_2022 <- f_data_sm %>%
  filter(SEASON == "2022", COUNTRY == "England") %>%
  group_by(AWAYTEAM) %>%
  summarise(MEAN_FTAG = mean(FTAG))

everton_fthg_mean <- england_home_2022 %>% 
  filter(HOMETEAM == "Everton") %>%
  pull(MEAN_FTHG)

mu_ftag_mean <- england_away_2022 %>% 
  filter(AWAYTEAM == "Man United") %>%
  pull(MEAN_FTAG)

rs <- rskellam(10000,mu1 = everton_fthg_mean, mu2 = mu_ftag_mean)
HTW <- sum(rs>0)/10000
D <- sum(rs == 0)/10000
ATW <- sum(rs<0)/10000

(coeff <- data.frame(HW = 1/HTW, D = 1/D, ATW = 1/ATW))
```

```{r}
data("f_data_sm")

get_poisson_form <- function(data, country){
  country_data <- f_data_sm %>% 
    filter(COUNTRY == country)
  
  country_data_home <- country_data %>% 
    group_by(HOMETEAM) %>%
    mutate(TEAM = HOMETEAM, OPPONENT = AWAYTEAM, GOAL = FTHG, HOME = 1) %>%
    ungroup() %>%
    select(TEAM, OPPONENT, GOAL, HOME)
  
  country_data_away <- country_data %>% 
    group_by(AWAYTEAM) %>%
    mutate(TEAM = AWAYTEAM, OPPONENT = HOMETEAM, GOAL = FTAG, HOME = 0) %>%
    ungroup() %>%
    select(TEAM, OPPONENT, GOAL, HOME)
  
  return(rbind(country_data_home, country_data_away))
}


england_2 <- get_poisson_form(f_data_sm, "England")

model <- glm(GOAL~TEAM+OPPONENT+HOME, data=england_2, family=poisson(link=log))

everton <- data.frame(TEAM = "Everton", OPPONENT = "Man United", HOME = 1)
mu <- data.frame(TEAM = "Man United", OPPONENT = "Everton", HOME = 0)

(pred_everton <- predict(model,newdata=everton,type="response"))
(pred_mu <- predict(model, newdata=mu, type="response"))
```

The poisson regression model did better, as in reality Man United won 2-1.  
The skellam distribution considered Everton as the favorite to win the game.

3. Define a metric to calculate the efficiency of the predictions. **(5 points)**

Let's divide the dataset into test and train sets.

```{r}
train <- f_data_sm %>% filter(SEASON!=max(SEASON))

train_poisson <- get_poisson_form(train, "England")

model <- glm(GOAL~TEAM+OPPONENT+HOME, data=train_poisson, family=poisson(link=log))

test_poisson <-get_poisson_form(f_data_sm %>% filter(SEASON == max(SEASON)), "England")

predicted <- predict(model,newdata=test_poisson,type="response")

test_poisson$P.G <- predicted

test_posson <- test_poisson %>%
  mutate(DIFF = GOAL - P.G)

sqrt(mean((test_poisson$GOAL - test_poisson$P.G)^2))

```

4. Find the under estimated and over estimated teams based on Poission model. **(5 points)**

```{r}
(test_poisson %>%
  filter(GOAL > P.G))

(test_poisson %>%
  filter(GOAL < P.G))
```

# Bradley terry model

## Problem 2(30 points)

### Construct Bradley-Terry model for NBA regular season games.


1. Load the dataset **nba_2009_2021** from the package **SportsAnalytics270** and remove the game Boston Celtics vs Indiana Pacers by filtering the **home.PTS** and **away.PTS** variables to be equal to 0.**(3 points)**

```{r}
nba2009_2021 <- nba2009_2021 %>%
  filter(home.PTS != 0, away.PTS != 0)
```

2. Prepare the dataset for fitting a Bradley-Terry model by adding 2 variables, **ht_w** and **at_w**.  
Assign the values of the varibles to (**ht_w** = 1, **at_w** = 0) if the home team won the game and   
(**ht_w** = 0, **at_w** = 1) if the away team won the game. **(5 points)**

```{r}
nba <- nba2009_2021 %>% select(SEASON_ID, home.TEAM_NAME, away.TEAM_NAME, home.WL) %>% 
          mutate(ht_w = ifelse(home.WL=="W",1,0),
                 at_w = ifelse(home.WL=="L",1,0),
                 home.TEAM_NAME = as.factor(home.TEAM_NAME),
                 away.TEAM_NAME = as.factor(away.TEAM_NAME))

train_nba <- nba %>% filter(SEASON_ID!="2021")  %>% 
        group_by(home.TEAM_NAME, away.TEAM_NAME) %>% 
        summarise(ht=sum(ht_w), at=sum(at_w))

test_nba <- nba %>% filter(SEASON_ID=="2021")  %>% 
        group_by(home.TEAM_NAME, away.TEAM_NAME) %>% 
        summarise(ht=sum(ht_w), at=sum(at_w))
```

3. Convert the variables representing the home team and the away team into a factor. **(2 points)**

```{r}
```

4. Fit a Bradley-Terry model into the dataset to get the abilities of the teams to win. **(5 points)**

```{r}
BT_Model <- BTm(cbind(ht,at), home.TEAM_NAME, away.TEAM_NAME, data=train_nba, id="team_")
```

```{r}
abilities <- abilities[order(abilities$ability, decreasing = T),]

ggplot(data=abilities, aes(x=reorder(team,ability), y = ability, fill =team))+ geom_bar(stat="identity") + coord_flip() + theme(legend.position = "none") + 
  labs(x="Teams", y="Ability to Win", title="Team vs Ability")
```

# Winning Percentage

## Pythagorean wins for european football

## Problem 3 (30 points)

1. Library **SportsAnalytics270** has a function final_table. It creates final league standing for the season. Use this function to create a dataframe with final standings of all seasons of your league. Combine seasons into 1 datafrmae. You need to get something like nba_east. **(10 points)**

```{r}
final_tables <- function(data = f_data_sm,country){
  result <- c()
  for(season in unique(data$SEASON)){
    season_table <- final_table(data, country, season)
    league <- data[data$SEASON == season & 
                     data$COUNTRY == country,]$LEAGUE[1]
    season_table$SEASON = season
    season_table$COUNTRY = country
    season_table$LEAGUE = league
    result <- rbind(result, season_table)
  }
  cols <- colnames(result)
  len <- length(cols)
  result <- result[c("SEASON","COUNTRY","LEAGUE",cols[1 : (len-3)])]
  return(as.data.frame(result))
}
england_tables <- final_tables(country = "England")
```

2. Create a variable for winning percentage and goal difference. Note, as there are draws in football, we are going to take draw as a half win. **(2 points)**
```{r}
calculate_wpct <- function(data){
  result <- c()
  for(index in 1:nrow(data)){
    team <- data[index,]
    team$WPCT <- (team$W) / (team$M)
    team$WPCTv2 <- (team$W + team$D/2)/(team$M)
    team$WPCTv3 <- (team$W + round(team$D / 3)) / (team$M)
    result <- rbind(result,team)
  }
  return(as.data.frame(result))
}


england_tables$GD <- england_tables$GF - england_tables$GA
england_tables$WPCT <- england_tables$W / (england_tables$M)

```

6. Build a regression model to estimate the value for k from the Pythagorean formula **(3 points)**

```{r}
england_tables_reg <- england_tables %>%
  filter(L != 0) %>%
  mutate(W = W + 0.5*D, L = L + 0.5*D, RATIO = GF / GA)

model <- lm(log(W/L)~0+log(RATIO), data=england_tables_reg)
summary(model)
```


5. Using the estimated value for k, calculate Pythagorean Winning percentage and Pythagorean wins for each team. **(3 points)**

```{r}
k <- model$coefficients[1]
head(england_tables <- england_tables %>%
  mutate(PWPCT = ( GF ^ k / (GF ^ k + GA ^ k)), PW = M * PWPCT),5)
```


6. Find over performing and under performing teams. **(2 points)**

```{r}
head(england_tables %>% 
  filter(W > PW),5)

head(england_tables %>%
    filter(W < PW),5)
```


# Elo Ratings
## Problem 4 (20 points)
### Building Elo rating model for NBA games.

1. Calculate the relative Elo ratings for all the games in the nba dataset.  
Make sure to adjust the ratings of the teams at the beginning of each season.  
This link https://fivethirtyeight.com/features/how-we-calculate-nba-elo-ratings/ shows the steps for calculating elo ratings in nba. **(10 points)**

```{r}
get_elos <- function(final_elos, def_elo = 1505){
  starting_elos <- c()
  if(length(final_elos) == 0){
    starting_elos = def_elo
  }
  else{
    starting_elos <- (def_elo * 0.25) + (final_elos * 0.75)
  }
  return(starting_elos)
}

make_final_elos_df <- function(final_elos){
  final_elos <- as.data.frame(final_elos)
  final_elos$TEAM <- rownames(final_elos)
  colnames(final_elos) <- c("ELO", "TEAM")
  rownames(final_elos) <- 1:length(final_elos$TEAM)
  final_elos <- final_elos[c("TEAM", "ELO")]
  return(final_elos)
}


nba_elos_relative <- function(data = nba2009_2018, home_factor, k_factor, def_elo = 1505){
  relative_df <- c()
  final_elos <- c()
  for(season in unique(data$SEASON_ID)){
    starting_elos <- get_elos(final_elos, def_elo)
    season_data <- data[data$SEASON_ID == season,]
    season_elos <- elo.run(score(home.PTS, away.PTS) ~
                             adjust(home.TEAM_NAME, home_factor) +
                             away.TEAM_NAME, data = season_data,
                           k = k_factor, initial.elos = starting_elos)
    season_final_elos <- final.elos(season_elos)
    season_elos <- data.frame(SEASON = season,season_elos)
    relative_df <- rbind(relative_df, season_elos)
    final_elos <- season_final_elos
  }
  final_elos <- make_final_elos_df(final_elos)
  return(list(relative = relative_df, elos_df = final_elos))
}


nba_rel_elos <- nba_elos_relative(nba2009_2021, 100, 20)
nba_rel_elos_df <- nba_rel_elos$elos_df
nba_rel_seasonal <- nba_rel_elos$relative
```

2. Interpret the predictive power of your model using either confusion matrix or brier score. **(5 points)**

```{r}
make_conf_matrix <- function(data = nba_rel_seasonal){
  rel_seasonal_conf <- table(Actual = data$wins.A, 
                           Predicted = data$Predicted)
  colnames(rel_seasonal_conf) <- c("Win", "Lose")
  rownames(rel_seasonal_conf) <- c("Win", "Lose")
  accuracy <- sum(diag(rel_seasonal_conf))/sum(rel_seasonal_conf)
  return(list(table = rel_seasonal_conf, accuracy = accuracy))
}

calculate_brier <- function(data = nba_rel_seasonal){
  diff <- data$p.A - data$wins.A
  accuracy <- sum(diff^2) / nrow(data)
  return(accuracy)
}

nba_rel_seasonal <- nba_rel_seasonal %>%
  mutate(Predicted = ifelse(p.A > 0.5,1,0))

(conf_seasonal <- confusionMatrix(data = factor(nba_rel_seasonal$wins.A),
                                            reference = factor(nba_rel_seasonal$Predicted)))

(calculate_brier(nba_rel_seasonal))

(make_conf_matrix(nba_rel_seasonal))

```
